content:
[0] A Bloomberg report yesterday suggested that the future Apple Watch lineup could see some pretty significant changes.

[1] The report specifically mentions that Apple is exploring models with a round face rather than the square one.

[2] Most smartwatches are round

[3] While square-faced watches have existed for over a century, traditional watches are predominantly round, and Android smartwatches are no different. Examples include:

  • [4] Amazfit Active Max
  • [5] Samsung Galaxy Watch 9
  • [6] Motorola Moto Watch
  • [7] All Garmin models (Venu, Epix Pro, Forerunner, Fenix)
  • [8] Google Pixel Watch

[9] Apple has always chosen a rectangular design, which makes it the outlier, so it wouldn't be surprising for the company to consider releasing a round Apple Watch in the future.

[10] There are also arguments for a round Apple Watch

[11] Apple's reasoning for choosing a rectangular design is that it can display more information. All the other screens we use daily — phones, tablets, laptops, monitors, and so on — are rectangular, and this is certainly no coincidence.

[12] Ultimately, this choice comes down to aesthetics versus practicality. Some people will always put practicality first, so the rectangular Apple Watch is definitely not going away. But on the other hand, there are also those who care deeply about appearance, and many people have a strong preference for round watches — whether traditional or smart.

[13] Additionally, not everyone who wears an Apple Watch needs to view a lot of information on the screen. Even if you rarely look at the screen, there are plenty of reasons to wear an Apple Watch, such as:

  • [14] Health and fitness monitoring
  • [15] Sleep tracking
  • [16] Emergency features like fall detection
  • [17] Contactless payments

[18] Of these, health and fitness monitoring is the biggest selling point for many people. If you're mainly not using your Apple Watch to view content, a round screen really isn't an issue for you at all.

[19] But the case for an Apple Ring is even stronger

[20] However, if you're the type of person who mainly uses an Apple Watch for health and fitness monitoring and doesn't really use it to view information, I'd say a smart ring is a much smarter choice.

[21] I personally switched from an Apple Watch to an Oura smart ring back in 2024, and recently upgraded to the fifth generation. What I love about it is that it's very discreet, allows me to keep wearing my favourite traditional watch, and only needs charging once a week.

[22] Almost two years ago, I already said I fully support replacing the Apple Watch with a smart ring, and I also believe Apple should release such a product. To this day, I still firmly believe in this view, and Gurman's report says Eddy Cue is also a huge fan of smart rings, so it looks like the chances of it happening are pretty good.

[23] I think it's possible Apple will release a round Apple Watch, but I lean more towards the idea that an Apple Ring will come first. What do you think? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
